messages:
kevin: FYI we're seeing a 30ms tail-latency spike from the logging pipeline in prod canary. CI green on main. Need quick decision: rollback or hotpatch? Also: how do we tag this so release tooling and changelogs stay sane?

tia: If rollback is simple, do that. If it's not (migrations or risky), hotpatch. For tagging, I prefer a clear patch bump on main, but pragmatic hotfix tags are fine if we backport.

alex: For rapid response I'm leaning hotpatch from the last release tag (v1.12.3) -> cherry-pick -> tag with a hotfix suffix, e.g. v1.12.3-hotfix.1, then later merge forward and cut v1.12.4 on main. Keeps main clean and avoids colliding with in-flight PRs.

maria: Note: our release-scraper currently only picks up `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`. Adding `-hotfix` will break the parser unless we relax the regex. I can patch the scraper quickly.

deploy-bot: deploy requested by kevin: staging -> prod-canary

ops-bot: Canary started (canary-3). Monitoring p95, p99, errors, logs.

kevin: Good call. Two proposals: (A) apply fix to main and bump patch to v1.12.4 (preferred for simplicity); (B) hotpatch v1.12.3-hotfix.1 and backport to main later. Which is less disruptive right now?

tia: Don't use buildmeta `+` in tags (e.g., v1.12.3+hotfix.1) 12 many tools ignore build metadata and some registries reject `+`. Either plain patch or `-hotfix` suffix.

alex: Practically, I'll create branch `hotfix/1.12.3`, cherry-pick the fix, tag `v1.12.3-hotfix.1`, run canary. If successful, merge the exact commit into main and cut `v1.12.4` in the next regular cycle.

maria: I'll update release-scraper regex from `^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+$` to `^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+(?:-[a-z]+\.\d+)?$` and prefer plain patch tags when computing changelogs. Will open a tiny PR now.

release-captain: Policy: critical SLA-impacting fixes can be hotpatched outside change windows. Rules: if fix merged to main first 12 tag as normal patch; if fix applied on a release branch and backported, use `-hotfix` suffix and record in incident doc. Document the path chosen.

kevin: Plan: create `hotfix/1.12.3` from tag v1.12.3, cherry-pick fix, tag `v1.12.3-hotfix.1`, run canary. If canary is healthy we'll promote and then ensure commit lands on main so we can cut v1.12.4 later. maria will update scraper so changelog includes hotfix tags.

alex: Typical commands:
```
git checkout -b hotfix/1.12.3 v1.12.3
git cherry-pick <commit-sha>
git tag -a v1.12.3-hotfix.1 -m "hotfix(logging): reduce tail latency"
git push origin hotfix/1.12.3
git push origin v1.12.3-hotfix.1
```
Then merge the fix into main and cut v1.12.4 when we're in the next bump window.

maria: PR opened: release-scraper: accept `-hotfix` tags. Small parser tweak included.

deploy-bot: Canary metrics: p95 back to baseline after ~12m, no error spikes. Promoting in 15m if stable.

tia: For changelog formatting, please use Conventional Commit style and add `[hotfix]` in the description, e.g. `fix(logging): reduce tail latency [hotfix]`. That makes it easy to filter.

kevin: Also add a short rollback playbook to the incident doc: revert for pure deploy-level regressions; rollforward for migrations or schema changes where revert is harmful.

release-captain: We should formalize this in a short RFC so teams stop debating ad-hoc. Assigning to alex + maria to draft the hotpatch semantics RFC (tags, automation, changelogs). Target: 2 weeks.

alex: ACK. I'll drop an RFC at docs/rfc/hotpatch-semantics.md and link back to this thread.

kevin: Proceeding with hotfix branch now. Will post updates here. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
